subject: Information Theory
title: Information Asymmetry in Markets
description: A micro-lesson that makes Information Asymmetry in Markets usable.

hook.text: A used car seller knows the car's flaws. You don't. Akerlof's 1970 paper showed this asymmetry can collapse markets.

buildup.text: Information asymmetry: one party knows more than the other. This creates adverse selection and moral hazard.

discovery.text: The market for 'lemons': buyers assume the worst, offer low prices, and good sellers exit. Only lemons remain.

twist.text: Solutions exist: warranties signal quality, reviews share information, and regulations require disclosure. All help.

climax.text: Digital platforms centralize information. Ratings on Amazon and Uber reduce buyer-seller asymmetry at massive scale.

punchline.text: Knowledge is power. Asymmetric knowledge is market failure.

quiz.question: What is the 'market for lemons' problem?
options: Information asymmetry drives good products out, leaving only bad ones
